newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao briefly arrested,freed in forgery case.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao briefly arrested,freed in forgery case.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao was arrested at his home in a criminal forgery case and then immediately released on bail, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Thursday.

The news agency said two officers of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) served an arrest warrant on Rao at his New Delhi residence late on Wednesday. But he immediately paid bail and was released.

The arrest warrant was issued last week by a New Delhi judge but had been temporarily suspended pending a ruling by the Delhi High Court on a plea by Rao for legal protection against arrest in the seven-year-old case.
Rao's forgery case dates from 1989. Federal police charged the former prime minister and five others with using false documents to defame a rival politician.

On Wednesday, the High Court granted Rao the right to pay pre-emptive, or anticipatory, bail which would last until a hearing into the forgery case which is set for next Monday. Rao has not commented publicly on the charges.
The High Court set a personal bond of 25,000 rupees ($700) and a surety of the same amount.
PTI said the wife of former foreign minister Pranab Mukherjee, who served in Rao's cabinet until the Congress party lost elections in May, paid the bail.
Rao stepped down as Congress leader last month after a judge upheld a summons ordering the politician to appear in court in a separate case of criminal conspiracy to cheat.
Rao says he is innocent of accusations he helped cheat a businessman of $100,000 in 1983.
A hearing in the cheating case has been scheduled for October 16.
